datasets.name: ds_daily
queryLines: SELECT date, region, category, order_count, return_count, revenue_usd, returns_usd FROM gold_daily_summary

datasets.name: ds_returns
queryLines: SELECT return_id, return_date, country, city, customer_lat, customer_lng, region, product_name, category, lot_id, facility, is_bad_lot, CASE WHEN is_bad_lot THEN 'Affected lot' ELSE 'Everyday returns' END AS source, return_reason, customer_comment, anger_score, CASE WHEN anger_score >= 0.9 THEN '3 - Very angry' WHEN anger_score >= 0.5 THEN '2 - Angry' WHEN anger_score >= 0.2 THEN '1 - Neutral' ELSE '0 - Satisfied' END AS sentiment, refund_amount_usd FROM gold_returns

datasets.name: ds_forecast
queryLines: WITH original AS ( SELECT DATE_TRUNC('WEEK', date) AS week, SUM(returns_usd) AS refunds FROM gold_daily_summary WHERE DATE_TRUNC('WEEK', date) < DATE_TRUNC('WEEK', current_date()) AND date >= DATEADD(day, -180, current_date()) GROUP BY 1), dates AS ( SELECT MAX(week) AS max_w FROM original), forecast AS ( SELECT week, refunds_forecast, refunds_upper, refunds_lower FROM AI_FORECAST(   TABLE(original),   horizon => (SELECT max_w + INTERVAL 28 DAYS FROM dates),   time_col => 'week',   value_col => 'refunds', parameters => '{"global_floor": 0}' )), actuals AS ( SELECT week, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS refunds_forecast,        CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS refunds_upper,        CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS refunds_lower, refunds FROM original), forecast_aligned AS ( SELECT week, refunds_forecast, refunds_upper, refunds_lower,        CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS refunds FROM forecast) SELECT week, refunds_forecast, refunds_upper, refunds_lower, refunds FROM actuals UNION ALL SELECT week, refunds_forecast, refunds_upper, refunds_lower, refunds FROM forecast_aligned UNION ALL SELECT (SELECT max_w FROM dates) AS week,        refunds AS refunds_forecast, refunds AS refunds_upper,        refunds AS refunds_lower, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS refunds FROM original WHERE week = (SELECT max_w FROM dates)

datasets.name: ds_sankey_flow
datasets.displayName: Category → product → top lot flow (long tails bucketed)
queryLines: WITH product_totals AS ( SELECT product_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM gold_returns GROUP BY product_name), top_products AS ( SELECT product_name FROM product_totals ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10), lot_totals AS ( SELECT lot_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM gold_returns GROUP BY lot_id), top_lots AS ( SELECT lot_id FROM lot_totals ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 15) SELECT category, CASE WHEN r.product_name IN (SELECT product_name FROM top_products) THEN r.product_name ELSE 'Other products' END AS product_name, CASE WHEN r.lot_id IN (SELECT lot_id FROM top_lots) THEN r.lot_id ELSE 'Other lots' END AS lot_id, COUNT(*) AS returns FROM gold_returns r GROUP BY category, CASE WHEN r.product_name IN (SELECT product_name FROM top_products) THEN r.product_name ELSE 'Other products' END, CASE WHEN r.lot_id IN (SELECT lot_id FROM top_lots) THEN r.lot_id ELSE 'Other lots' END

lines:
# LuxeBeauty Returns — Operations

**The story** — weekly refunds spiked to ~$180K three weeks ago (3× our $60K baseline). Cause: production lot **LOT-2026-0427** of three Skincare SKUs (SKU-1001/1002/1003) released from Lyon despite a QC note about texture variations. ~250 customers affected, concentrated EU (Paris > London > Milan).

**What to see** — KPI sparklines carry the spike-then-decay shape · forecast-line marks the production-incident date as a vertical bar to the LEFT of the bump (cause → effect → 4-week recovery forecast) · donut shows Skincare dominates refunds · bubble map lights up Europe with Paris deepest red.

# Investigation — why is this happening?

**Same data, split by the dimensions that matter** — which products, which lots, which countries, what customers are saying. 

The story emerges: 3 Skincare SKUs sit an order of magnitude above the rest · all on ONE lot (`LOT-2026-0427`, \~10× any other) · the affected-lot bars dwarf everyday returns in every EU country and `quality` is the dominant reason · `ai_classify` puts most affected-lot comments into Angry / Very angry · the comments cluster on "grainy", "separated", "watery".

Click any **'Affected lot'** bar to filter every other widget on the page.
